researchQuestion: Close the active-batch loss/cash-burn, dilution/acquisition-accounting normalization gate using the latest primary 10-Q.
exactUnresolvedGate: loss/cash-burn, dilution/acquisition-accounting normalization and Neutron qualification/schedule risk remain
summary: Latest Q2 2026 primary filing materially closes the financing/dilution and acquisition-accounting portion of the RKLB gate. Rocket Lab had $2.129B cash plus $258.1M marketable securities at June 30, 2026, while first-half net loss was $94.3M. Financing cash inflow was dominated by $1.530B of ATM equity proceeds. The filing also records $160.8M of common stock issued in connection with acquisitions and identifies the April 2026 Mynaric acquisition consideration as 2.277M shares plus nominal cash. Current potentially dilutive securities excluded from EPS included 13.096M options/RSUs, 2.608M shares underlying convertible notes, and 7.451M shares underlying collared forwards. This supports a high-confidence dilution normalization, but Neutron schedule/qualification risk remains a separate unresolved technical/program gate.

evidence.fact: At June 30, 2026 Rocket Lab reported $2.129B cash and cash equivalents and $258.1M marketable securities; first-half 2026 net loss was $94.280M.
evidence.sourceLocation: Balance sheet, cash-flow statement and liquidity discussion

evidence.fact: First-half 2026 ATM equity offering proceeds were $1.529639B with $16.722M issuance costs.
evidence.sourceLocation: Cash flows from financing activities, filing lines 393-400

evidence.fact: The company issued common stock with $160.802M fair value in connection with acquisitions during first-half 2026.
Rocket Lab completed the Mynaric acquisition on April 14, 2026 for aggregate consideration of $155.3M, consisting of nominal cash and 2,277,002 common shares.

Potentially dilutive securities disclosed at June 30, 2026 included 13.09552M stock options/RSUs, 2.607745M shares underlying convertible senior notes, and 7.4512M shares underlying collared forward transactions.

inference: Near-term solvency/cash-runway risk is low on current liquidity, but the business remains materially dependent on capital markets in economic substance because 2026 liquidity growth was overwhelmingly equity-financing driven rather than internally generated cash.
Dilution normalization should treat ATM issuance, acquisition shares, equity awards, convertible-note shares and collared-forward shares separately to avoid double-counting.
unknowns: Current Neutron qualification state, schedule confidence and remaining program-critical milestones are not closed by the financial filing and remain a separate gate.
Future opportunistic financing remains explicitly possible per company liquidity disclosure.
falsifiers: A later filing showing material reversal of liquidity or substantially higher cash burn.
A primary program disclosure showing Neutron milestones materially behind or ahead of the current underwriting assumption.
